p:cNvPr.descr: An image illustrating the properties of the covalent bond between cobalt and C-5' of the deoxyadenosyl group. This image begins with 5’-deoxyadenosine, which begins with a pink pentagon with thick sides on the bottom three sides. From the top point, clockwise, the first point is O. The second point is H bonding down to CH2. There is a 4’ at the point, and a 5’ before CH2. At the third point HO (inside the pentagon) bonds down to H. There is a 3’ at this point. The fourth point has OH (inside the pentagon) bonding down to H. There is a 2’ at this point. The fifth point has H bonding down to N. There is a 1’ at this point. N is the top point of a pentagon. The third point also has an N. There is a double bond on the right bottom side. The left side of the pentagon shares a side with the right side of a hexagon with alternating double-bonded sides, beginning with that shared side. An N is at the top point, and an N is at the bottom left point. The bottom point bonds down to NH2. This is all in pink. CH2 above bonds down to CO3+ (in pink) in the middle of the Corrin ring system. This system has three irregular blue pentagons on the left and three irregular pentagons on the right. There are two irregular hexagons between the pentagons on each side. The top row has a pentagon on the left. At the top point, C double bonds up and left to O, bonds up and right to NH2, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH3 (in blue, inside the pentagon). The left point of this pentagon bonds up and left to H and bonds down and left to CH2, which bonds down and left to CH2, which bonds down and left to C, which double bonds up and left to O and down and right to H2N. The bottom left side has a thick line. There is a blue hexagon that shares sides with this pentagon to the right; this side is double bonded and has an N at the bottom. This N has a red arrow pointing to CO3+ in the middle. The top point of this hexagon bonds up to CH3. This hexagon also has a double-bonded side on the top right, and an N on the bottom right point. This hexagon shares sides with a blue pentagon to the right. This pentagon has a thick bottom left and bottom right side. The top of this pentagon bonds up and left to H, and bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to C, which double bonds up and left to O and bonds up and right to NH2. The point to the right of that bonds down to CH3 and up and right to CH2, which bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to O and bonds down and right to NH2. In the second row, is a hexagon that shares sides with the first pentagon and a pentagon below. The top left and bottom sides are double-bonded. It shares the N described in the first pentagon and has an n on the bottom right side, which has a red arrow pointing to CO3+ in the middle. The two red arrows coming from the Ns for the top right and bottom right sides of this hexagon. To the right is a hexagon whose left point is the CO3+ in the middle. This hexagon shares an N on the top left point, shares a thick side with the second pentagon described above, and has an almost vertical right side, the goes left to N, which has a red arrow pointing to CO3+ in the middle. The bottom right point bonds up and right to H. In the last row, to the left, a pentagon shares the top side, which is double-bonded, with the hexagon described in the second row. On the left point it bonds up and left to H3C and down and left to H3C. The bottom point bonds up to H (inside the pentagon) and down and left to CH2, which bonds down and left to CH2, which bonds down and left to C. C double bonds up and right to O and down and right to H2N. To the right of this is a hexagon with thick lines on the bottom left and bottom right sides. The bottom point bonds down and right to CH3. This hexagon share an N with those above at the top left and top right sides. It also has a double bonded side on the bottom left and right sides. The right side is shared with the last pentagon in the Corrin ring system. This pentagon has thick sides on the bottom left and bottom right. The right point bonds down and right to H and up and right to CH2, which bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to O and down and right to NH2. The bottom point bonds up to H3C (still in blue and in the pentagon) and down and right to CH2, which bonds down and right to CH2, which bonds down to C, which double bonds left to O and bonds down to NH. NH bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to HC, which bonds right to CH3 for amino-isopropanol. HC also bonds down to O (where a tan box begins), which bonds down to P, which bonds right to O- and double bonds down to O. P also bonds left to O, which sits above a pentagon’s right side and bonds down to H at the third point of the pentagon (with the first point being the top point and going clockwise). This pentagon has thick sides on the bottom three sides. The top point is O. The second point has H bonding down to CH2OH. The fourth point has OH (inside the pentagon) bonding down to H. The fifth point has H bonding up to N, where N is the bottom point of a pentagon. This pentagon has a double bond on the top right side and N at the top point, which has a dashed black arrow pointing up through the hexagon in the middle of the third row in the Corrin ring system. This arrow turns sold red and points to CO3+ in the middle. Next to the pentagon with the Ns is a blank hexagon, which shares its right side with the left side of the pentagon just previously discussed. It has double-bonded sides on the top and bottom left. The top left point bonds up and left to H3C and the bottom left point bonds down and left to H3C. This is all in a tan box and represents dimethyl-benzimidazole ribonucleotide.
